title: Note for the Council (Environment) AOB item on high-voltage switchgear, document 10693/1/26 REV 1
key_claim: Three member states (Italy, Bulgaria, Czech Republic) tell the Environment Council that the F-gas Regulation's bans come into force in 2028 (2032 for high-voltage); that a fluoronitrile-based device with lower life-cycle impact than dry air and vacuum is currently non-compliant; that the EU has 2 EU-based fluoronitrile suppliers and 1 EU-based dry-air supplier; that if fluoronitrile disappears one dry-air maker remains with capacity below EU demand; and they ask for a stop-the-clock provision in the Omnibus or Grid package.
frame_summary: The note argues that the F-gas Regulation's 2028 bans, as written, would bar a lower-impact fluoronitrile route and leave Europe's high-voltage grid buyers dependent on one EU dry-air supplier, so the clock should be stopped until a proper life-cycle assessment is done.
verbatim_quote: only one manufacturer of dry-air solutions remains with a manufacturing capacity lower than the European demand
verbatim_list: the EU market today consists of 2 EU-based suppliers of fluoronitrile solutions and 1 EU-based supplier of dry-air solutions
which is currently non-compliant under the provisions of the F-Gas Regulation
Provide a stop the clock provision for the ban of SF6-free equipment containing fluoronitrile, in the Omnibus package or the Grid package.
already approaches €1 billion per year and could exceed €3 billion by 2030
the bans set out in the F-gas Regulation come into force in 2028
notes: Tier 1 primary: Council General Secretariat note for the 25 June 2026 Environment Council AOB item. Advocacy position of three delegations, not a Council decision; used as the primary statement of the legal and supply position and as the one structural anchor (97 days old at scan date). title: SF6 replacement: from regulatory pressure to industrial deployment challenges
key_claim: Reporting on CIGRE 2026, the SuperGrid Institute says several manufacturers showed SF6-free installations operating up to 420 kV and even 550 kV, most industrial momentum comes from European markets, many other countries rely on reporting rather than bans, and keeping equipment compact without raising gas pressure remains a main technical challenge.
frame_summary: The Institute argues that SF6 replacement has moved from a regulatory objective to an industrial deployment problem, with credible technologies at up to 550 kV but unresolved engineering trade-offs and a Europe-led regulatory push.
verbatim_quote: Several manufacturers presented or referenced installations operating up to 420 kV and even 550 kV
verbatim_list: As a result, most of the industrial momentum currently comes from European markets
Many countries, including Canada, Japan, South Korea, the United Kingdom and Australia, currently rely primarily on reporting
maintaining compact equipment without significantly increasing gas pressure remains one of the industry's main technical challenges
notes: Tier 2: research institute (French energy-transition technology institute) authored by Emmanuelle Beguery; published 2026-09-24, modified 2026-09-25. The article carries no 2028/2032 dates, PFAS references or supplier counts; used as the sourced counter-evidence that the technology is deployable.

title: Hitachi Energy Expands SF6-Free Switchgear Portfolio at CIGRE 2026
key_claim: Hitachi Energy said more than 4,000 EconiQ SF6-free units have been ordered by customers in 40 countries, including TenneT Germany's order for the EconiQ 420 kV, 80 kA live tank circuit breaker; the article does not say which gas technology the portfolio uses.
frame_summary: The trade report presents SF6-free high-voltage equipment as commercially mature, with a vendor citing thousands of units ordered across 40 countries.
verbatim_quote: The company said more than 4,000 EconiQ units have been ordered by customers in 40 countries.
verbatim_list: German transmission system operator TenneT Germany has ordered the EconiQ 420 kV, 80 kA live tank circuit breaker
notes: Tier 3 specialist trade press reporting a vendor claim; the 4,000-unit figure is the vendor's own. Article does not name the replacement gas.

title: GE Vernova completes its SF6-free gas-insulated switchgear range with new 170 kV product launched at CIGRE Paris 2026
key_claim: GE Vernova launched a 170 kV SF6-free gas-insulated switchgear completing a range across 72.5, 145, 170, 245 and 420 kV; the product is available for order now, manufactured in Europe. The article does not mention fluoronitrile or PFAS.
frame_summary: The report treats the launch as completion of a full SF6-free transmission range, framing the remaining challenge as equipment design rather than finding an insulating gas.
verbatim_quote: The F35g 170 kV is available for order now, manufactured in Europe.
notes: Tier 3 specialist trade press relaying a vendor launch (26 August 2026, CIGRE Paris). Byline Kelly Lippke.

title: LIFE Blue 420 kV GIS: emission-free 420 kV gas-insulated switchgear with clean air insulation and vacuum switching
key_claim: Siemens Energy and Elia's EU-funded LIFE partnership, started October 2024 and scheduled to run to September 2028, will pilot a completely F-gas-free 420 kV GIS using clean air and vacuum switching at Elia's Vilvoorde substation, with 270 replications planned by 2032.
frame_summary: The vendor page presents the clean-air, vacuum-switching 420 kV GIS as a demonstration project whose commercial replication is planned for the early 2030s.
verbatim_quote: This Blue GIS will replace an existing indoor GIS at TSO Elia in Vilvoorde, Belgium.
verbatim_list: Siemens Energy and ELIA entered a partnership in October 2024, which is scheduled to continue until September 2028.
270 replications of the project throughout Europe and worldwide are planned by 2032
